chief_complaint: blood pressure 146/94 and proteinuria after 20 weeks
hpi_details: 31-year-old female, G1P0 at 34 weeks gestation, presents for a routine prenatal visit. She has no complaints, no headache, and no visual changes. However, her blood pressure today is 148/96 mmHg, and a urine dipstick shows 2+ proteinuria.
ideas: She thinks her blood pressure spiked only because she rushed up two flights of stairs in a panic after getting stuck in traffic.
concerns: She is worried that her doctor will admit her to the hospital or place her on strict bed rest today, preventing her from completing her final week at work before maternity leave.
expectations: She hopes to rest quietly in the exam room so her blood pressure can be rechecked and confirmed normal before going home.
social_hx: Non-smoker; no alcohol or recreational drug use during pregnancy

available_results.collected_at: At prenatal triage before clinician assessment

clinical_knowledge.topic: Preeclampsia (mild/without severe features) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Preeclampsia (mild/without severe features) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Pre-eclampsia mild: Close monitoring of BP and fetal growth, deliver at 37 weeks, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: blood pressure 146/94 and proteinuria after 20 weeks
Key HPI features: 31-year-old G1P0 at 34 weeks gestation with confirmed blood pressure of 148/96 mmHg and 2+ proteinuria; she denies headache and visual changes.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Pre-eclampsia mild.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Preeclampsia (mild/without severe features).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Chronic hypertension without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring warning signs of progression to severe features in new hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria.
management_principles: Plan for Pre-eclampsia mild: Close monitoring of BP and fetal growth, deliver at 37 weeks
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: blood pressure 146/94 and proteinuria after 20 weeks

31-year-old female, G1P0 at 34 weeks gestation, presents for a routine prenatal visit. She has no complaints, no headache, and no visual changes. However, her blood pressure today is 148/96 mmHg, and a urine dipstick shows 2+ proteinuria.
reference_soap.objective: BP 148/96 (repeated and confirmed 4 hours later). Fundal height 34 cm. Fetal heart rate 145 bpm, reactive non-stress test. Urine dipstick 2+ protein. Edema 1+ in bilateral lower extremities. No RUQ tenderness.
reference_soap.plan: Admit to obstetrics for maternal and fetal monitoring. Obtain comprehensive preeclampsia labs (CBC, AST/ALT, Creatinine, 24-hour urine protein or Spot UPC ratio). Plan for delivery at 37 weeks unless severe features develop.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Pre-eclampsia mild
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Pre-eclampsia mild
Implement evidence-based management plan: Close monitoring of BP and fetal growth, deliver at 37 weeks

teaching.one_liner: Pregnant patient at 34 weeks with confirmed blood pressure of 148/96 mmHg and proteinuria.
red_flags: New hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria; assess urgently for progression to severe features

must_ask.objective: Explain monitoring plan and delivery timing
must_ask.say: We'll monitor your blood pressure and the baby's growth closely, and plan delivery around 37 weeks.

history.answer: I came in for my regular prenatal checkup, but the nurse told me my blood pressure was 148 over 96 and they found protein in my urine.
I am exactly 34 weeks pregnant today, and my due date is six weeks from now.
I have attended every scheduled prenatal checkup on time, and all my visits up until today were completely normal.
I have not had any falls, abdominal trauma, recent sex, or strenuous physical exertion.
No, I have not noticed any vaginal bleeding, spotting, or blood clots.
No, my belly feels soft and relaxed, with no painful cramps or tightening contractions.
No, I have not had any fluid or water leaking from my vagina.
Yes, the baby has been moving around normally and actively today, just like usual.
No, I have not had any headaches at all.
No, my vision has been completely clear with no blurriness, dark spots, or flashes of light.
No, I do not have any pain under my ribs, in my stomach, or on my right side.
history.topic: Epigastric or right upper quadrant pain

history.answer: My feet and ankles swell up a little bit by the end of the day, but my face and hands have not felt puffy.
No, I have not had any shortness of breath, chest tightness, or racing heartbeats.
history.topic: Shortness of breath or chest pain

history.answer: No, I have not felt dizzy, lightheaded, or faint.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge.
All my ultrasounds have been normal; at 20 weeks the baby was growing well and the placenta was in a safe location.
Before this pregnancy and during my earlier visits, my blood pressure was always around 110 over 70.
All my earlier blood tests and my one-hour glucose screening for gestational diabetes came back normal.
No, I haven't had excessive thirst or frequent urination, and I've gained about 22 pounds steadily so far.
This is my very first pregnancy; I have never been pregnant before and have had no miscarriages.
I have never had high blood pressure, diabetes, kidney disease, or any chronic health conditions.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I only take a daily prenatal multivitamin with iron; I don't take any prescription or over-the-counter medicines.
I do not have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used e-cigarettes.
I do not drink alcohol and have never used any recreational drugs.
I work as an accountant at an office and live at home with my husband.
My mother developed mild high blood pressure in her late fifties, but no one in my family had hypertension during pregnancy.
I had to sprint up the stairs because I was running late from heavy traffic, so I figured my pressure was temporarily high from all that rushing.
I am worried you are going to admit me or put me on strict bed rest today, right when I have one final week left at work to finish my projects.
I am hoping that if I sit quietly for a few minutes we can take my blood pressure again and I will be cleared to go home.

exam.finding: Alert, well-appearing pregnant female sitting comfortably in no acute distress.
Blood pressure 148/96 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
Visual fields full to confrontation; fundoscopy shows sharp optic disc margins with no papilledema, hemorrhages, or exudates.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with normal vesicular breath sounds and no crackles or wheezes.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Gravid abdomen consistent with a third-trimester gestation; fundal height measures 34 cm.
Fetal heart rate is 145 beats/min with regular rhythm; normal active bowel sounds heard throughout maternal abdomen.
Uterus is soft and non-tender with no contractions; abdomen is soft without right upper quadrant or epigastric tenderness.
1+ pitting edema noted over the bilateral lower legs and ankles; no calves tenderness or erythema.
Patellar and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally with no inducible clonus.
Sterile speculum exam shows a closed cervix with no vaginal bleeding, fluid pooling, or discharge.
